rv.q: You have probably wondered what it would be like to walk a mile (or a light-year) in the hair coils of Princess Leia, the intergalactic pinup girl from the original “Star Wars” movies. O.K., so you haven’t.
She makes an expert witness to fame in all its ridiculousness and peril, who knows that celebrity is "obscurity biding its time."
Fisher's material is funny enough, and her delivery appealingly loose and conversational. But the show feels more like an extended therapy session than a polished piece of theater.
No surprise. I did hate it. It’s rather like bad tell-all late night TV.

cn.t: Fisher's witty, self-deprecating memoir wins over most critics with its clever humor about Hollywood dysfunction, though some find the candor too selective and the celebrity confessional format grating.

vs.sum: The legendary former nightclub retains a distinctive atmosphere even in its theatrical configuration. However, comfort is among the worst on Broadway — the rear mezzanine is extremely steep with limited guardrails and tight legroom throughout both levels.

acc.note: No elevator to Mezzanine. 10 induction loops. 81 assistive listening devices. Orchestra wheelchair seating.
